slots.practicalActivity: In the Azure portal (or a free Azure subscription), browse to the Data Factory service to see its creation blade without yet creating one, then write a short comparison identifying 2 concrete transformation steps in a hypothetical pipeline that would be "transform-then-load" (ETL) versus "load-then-transform" (ELT).
slots.deliverable: A short written ETL-vs-ELT comparison naming 2 concrete transformation steps and which pattern each belongs to, plus confirmation you located the Data Factory creation blade in the Azure portal.

lessons.title: Data Factory vs. SSIS vs. Fabric Data Factory

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page comparison table of Azure Data Factory, SSIS, and Fabric Data Factory covering hosting model, pricing model, and typical use case for each.
slots.deliverable: A one-page comparison table (ADF vs. SSIS vs. Fabric Data Factory) covering hosting, pricing, and use case for each.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Azure portal, create a real Azure Data Factory instance (or confirm an existing one), open Data Factory Studio, and tour the Author, Monitor, and Manage hubs, noting what each is used for.
slots.deliverable: A live Data Factory instance with Data Factory Studio opened, plus a short written note identifying the purpose of the Author, Monitor, and Manage hubs.

slots.practicalActivity: In Data Factory Studio, create a Linked Service connecting to an Azure Blob Storage (or ADLS Gen2) account, testing the connection successfully.
slots.deliverable: A successfully tested Linked Service in Data Factory Studio pointing at a real Azure Storage account.

lessons.title: Connecting to Azure SQL & On-Premises SQL Server

slots.practicalActivity: Create a second Linked Service connecting to an Azure SQL Database (or on-premises SQL Server via a connection string), then create a Dataset on top of each Linked Service — one blob/file dataset and one SQL table dataset — importing the schema for each.
slots.deliverable: Two Datasets (one file-based, one SQL-based), each with an imported schema, built on top of two different Linked Services.

slots.practicalActivity: Parameterize the file-based Dataset from the previous slot so its file path is driven by a pipeline parameter instead of being hardcoded, then test it by passing two different parameter values.
slots.deliverable: A parameterized Dataset successfully pointed at two different files by passing two different parameter values.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new pipeline in Data Factory Studio and add a Copy activity that copies data from the file Dataset to the SQL Dataset built in the previous chapter, running it in Debug mode.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline with a working Copy activity, successfully run in Debug mode, moving real data from a file into a SQL table.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the Copy activity's mapping tab and manually map at least one column differently than the default inference, then add a Lookup activity before it that retrieves a single configuration value from a SQL table, and a Stored Procedure activity after it that logs the run.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline with a manual column mapping on the Copy activity, preceded by a working Lookup activity and followed by a Stored Procedure activity call.

lessons.title: Web, Wait, Fail & Set Variable Activities

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Set Variable activity to capture the Lookup's output, a Wait activity for a short delay, and a Web activity calling a simple public API, chaining them together with the Copy activity from before into one complete first pipeline.
slots.deliverable: One complete end-to-end pipeline chaining Lookup, Set Variable, Wait, Web, and Copy activities, successfully run start to finish in Debug mode.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: without referring back to the lesson videos, rebuild this chapter's first end-to-end pipeline from scratch in a new pipeline canvas, adding a Fail activity on one branch that triggers if the Lookup value doesn't meet a condition you define.
slots.deliverable: An original rebuilt pipeline (not copy-pasted) demonstrating Copy, Lookup, Set Variable, and a conditional Fail activity, run successfully in Debug mode.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a pipeline-level parameter and a pipeline-level variable to your Chapter 3 pipeline, then add an If Condition activity branching based on the parameter's value, and a Switch activity handling 3 possible values of a status variable.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline with one parameter, one variable, a working If Condition branch, and a Switch activity handling 3 distinct cases.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a ForEach activity that loops over an array of 3 file names (via a Lookup or a hardcoded array) running the Copy activity once per file, then add an Until activity that polls a variable in a loop until it reaches a target value.
slots.deliverable: A working ForEach activity that runs Copy 3 times over an array, plus a separate Until activity loop that exits once its condition is met.

slots.practicalActivity: Split your pipeline into a parent and a child pipeline using an Execute Pipeline activity, passing parameters from parent to child, and use at least 2 Data Factory expression language functions (e.g., utcnow(), pipeline().RunId) somewhere in the pipeline.
slots.deliverable: A parent pipeline calling a child pipeline via Execute Pipeline Activity with passed parameters, using at least 2 system variables or expression functions.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: build one original orchestration pipeline using all of this chapter's control-flow activities together — an If Condition deciding whether to run a ForEach loop over a parameterized list of items, with an Until activity polling for completion and an Execute Pipeline activity calling a child pipeline for the final step.
slots.deliverable: One original control-flow pipeline combining If Condition, ForEach, Until, and Execute Pipeline Activity, run successfully in Debug mode.

lessons.title: What Is a Mapping Data Flow?

slots.practicalActivity: Create a new Mapping Data Flow, turn on Data Flow Debug mode, and add a Source transformation pointed at one of your Chapter 2 Datasets, confirming the Data Preview tab shows real rows.
slots.deliverable: A new Mapping Data Flow with Debug mode on and a Source transformation showing live Data Preview rows from a real dataset.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Sink transformation writing to a different Dataset than the Source, then insert a Filter transformation (e.g., excluding null or zero-value rows), a Select transformation dropping 2 unneeded columns, and a Derived Column transformation computing one new calculated column.
slots.deliverable: A data flow with Source, Filter, Select, Derived Column, and Sink transformations chained together, verified in Data Preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Join transformation combining your data flow's stream with a second Source (e.g., a lookup dataset), an Aggregate transformation grouping and summing a numeric column, and a Conditional Split transformation routing rows into two different Sinks based on a condition.
slots.deliverable: A data flow extended with a Join, an Aggregate, and a Conditional Split routing rows to 2 separate Sinks, all verified in Data Preview.

slots.practicalActivity: Open the data flow's Optimize tab and change the partitioning strategy (e.g., switch from default to a fixed partition count) on one transformation, then run the pipeline containing the data flow and compare the execution duration shown in Monitor before and after the change.
slots.deliverable: A before/after comparison of data flow execution time in Monitor after changing a partitioning setting on the Optimize tab.

slots.practicalActivity: Chapter-ending lab: build one original Mapping Data Flow from scratch combining Filter, Derived Column, Join, Aggregate, and Conditional Split transformations against real data from your earlier Datasets, wrap it in a pipeline with a Data Flow activity, and run it end to end.
slots.deliverable: One original Mapping Data Flow (Filter + Derived Column + Join + Aggregate + Conditional Split) wrapped in a pipeline, successfully executed end to end.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Schedule trigger that would run one of your pipelines daily at a fixed time, and separately create a Tumbling Window trigger with a defined window size on a pipeline that uses WindowStart/WindowEnd system variables, publishing both.
slots.deliverable: A published Schedule trigger and a published Tumbling Window trigger, each correctly attached to a pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a Storage Event trigger that fires a pipeline when a new blob is created in a container, test it by uploading a file, then chain a second pipeline to run only after the first trigger's pipeline succeeds using trigger dependencies.
slots.deliverable: A working Storage Event trigger proven by uploading a test file, plus a chained trigger dependency running a second pipeline afterward.

slots.practicalActivity: In the Manage hub, inspect the default Azure Integration Runtime attached to your Data Factory, noting its region and the activities it's currently running, then create a second Azure IR with a different region setting.
slots.deliverable: A screenshot or note identifying the default Azure IR's region, plus a second custom Azure IR created with an explicit region.

slots.practicalActivity: Walk through (or, if you have a spare machine, actually perform) the Self-Hosted IR setup: generate the authentication key in Data Factory Studio, and document the exact steps you'd take to install and register it on an on-premises machine to securely reach a local SQL Server.
slots.deliverable: A generated Self-Hosted IR authentication key plus a written step-by-step install/registration plan for connecting it to an on-premises SQL Server.

slots.practicalActivity: Run several of your existing pipelines, then use the Monitor hub to inspect their run history, drilling into one run's activity-level details; set a retry policy (count and interval) on one Copy activity and configure an Azure Monitor alert for pipeline failures.
slots.deliverable: A Monitor hub screenshot showing at least 2 pipeline runs with activity-level detail, plus a configured retry policy and one Azure Monitor alert rule for failures.

slots.practicalActivity: Add an error-handling path to one pipeline (e.g., an "on failure" dependency condition leading to a notification or logging activity), and connect your Data Factory's diagnostic settings to send pipeline run logs to a Log Analytics workspace, then run a Kusto query against the logged data.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline with an on-failure error-handling branch, plus one working Kusto query against pipeline logs in Log Analytics.

lessons.title: Dataflow Gen2 vs. Mapping Data Flows

slots.practicalActivity: In a Microsoft Fabric workspace, create a new Dataflow Gen2, connecting it to a simple data source, and write a short comparison of how its Power Query-based experience differs from the Mapping Data Flow canvas used earlier in this course.
slots.deliverable: A created Dataflow Gen2 in a Fabric workspace, plus a short written comparison against the Mapping Data Flow experience.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a pipeline in Fabric Data Factory with a Copy activity, setting OneLake as the destination (writing into a Lakehouse's Files or Tables area), and run it to confirm the data lands in OneLake.
slots.deliverable: A Fabric pipeline with a Copy activity that successfully writes data into a OneLake Lakehouse.

lessons.title: When to Choose ADF vs. Fabric

slots.practicalActivity: Export one of your earlier ADF pipelines and walk through Fabric's pipeline import/migration experience to recreate it in Fabric Data Factory, then write a short decision memo on when you'd choose ADF vs. Fabric Data Factory for a hypothetical new project.
slots.deliverable: A pipeline recreated in Fabric Data Factory from an earlier ADF pipeline, plus a short written ADF-vs-Fabric decision memo.

slots.practicalActivity: Lab: build one original pipeline directly in Fabric Data Factory (not migrated) that reads from a Dataflow Gen2 output and writes to OneLake, running it end to end inside the Fabric workspace.
slots.deliverable: One original Fabric Data Factory pipeline, built from scratch, successfully moving data from a Dataflow Gen2 into OneLake.

slots.practicalActivity: Enable a system-assigned managed identity on your Data Factory, store a connection secret in Azure Key Vault, and update one Linked Service to retrieve that secret via Key Vault instead of storing it directly; then assign an RBAC role scoping a teammate (or a second test account) to Data Factory Contributor only.
slots.deliverable: A Linked Service pulling its secret from Key Vault via the Data Factory's managed identity, plus one RBAC role assignment scoped to Data Factory Contributor.

slots.practicalActivity: Connect your Data Factory to a Git repository (Azure DevOps or GitHub) through Manage > Git configuration, commit your pipelines to a feature branch, and publish from the collaboration branch into a "live" factory version, documenting the dev/test/prod environment pattern this enables.
slots.deliverable: A Data Factory connected to Git with pipelines committed to a branch, plus a documented publish into the live/ARM-deployed version and a written note on the dev/test/prod pattern.

slots.practicalActivity: Export your Data Factory's ARM template (Manage > ARM Template > Export), review the generated JSON to identify where a Linked Service's connection string parameter lives, and outline the Azure DevOps release pipeline stages you'd use to deploy that template from dev to prod.
slots.deliverable: An exported ARM template JSON file with the Linked Service parameter identified, plus a written outline of the Azure DevOps release pipeline stages for dev-to-prod deployment.

lessons.title: Capstone: Connect & Build the Copy Pipeline

slots.practicalActivity: Write a one-page business requirements document for a capstone data pipeline (e.g., ingesting daily sales files into a reporting table), then build the Linked Services, Datasets, and the initial Copy activity pipeline that satisfies the ingestion half of those requirements.
slots.deliverable: A one-page capstone requirements document, plus a working Copy pipeline (Linked Services + Datasets + Copy activity) implementing the ingestion requirement.

lessons.title: Capstone: Add Control Flow & Error Handling

slots.practicalActivity: Extend the capstone pipeline with control-flow activities (If Condition and/or ForEach as the requirements call for) and an error-handling branch (on-failure path with logging or a Fail activity), run it, and deliberately trigger the failure path once to confirm it works.
slots.deliverable: The capstone pipeline extended with control flow and a proven error-handling branch (one deliberate failure-path run captured in Monitor).

lessons.title: Capstone: Build the Mapping Data Flow

slots.practicalActivity: Add a Mapping Data Flow to the capstone pipeline that cleans and transforms the ingested data (filtering, derived columns, and at least one aggregate or join as your requirements call for) before it reaches its final destination.
slots.deliverable: A Mapping Data Flow integrated into the capstone pipeline, transforming real ingested data before its final load.

slots.practicalActivity: Attach an appropriate trigger (schedule or event-based) to the finished capstone pipeline, secure its credentials via Key Vault/managed identity, and set up a retry policy plus a Monitor-hub check, running the full pipeline end to end once under the trigger.
slots.deliverable: The capstone pipeline running end to end under a real trigger, with Key Vault-based credentials and a visible successful run in Monitor.

slots.practicalActivity: Prepare and deliver a short walkthrough (written or recorded) of the finished capstone pipeline: the business problem, the architecture (Linked Services, Datasets, activities, data flow, trigger), and one thing you'd improve with more time.
slots.deliverable: A short capstone presentation (written summary or recording) covering the problem, the architecture, and one planned improvement.

slots.practicalActivity: Capstone retrospective: compare your finished pipeline against your original requirements document line by line, noting which requirements were fully met, partially met, or deferred, and write one paragraph on how you'd re-scope the project if starting over with what you know now.
slots.deliverable: A written line-by-line requirements-vs-delivered comparison plus a one-paragraph re-scoping reflection.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can build, secure, schedule, and monitor real multi-activity data pipelines in both Azure Data Factory and Microsoft Fabric Data Factory -- including mapping data flow transformations, Git-based CI/CD, and a complete capstone pipeline -- the orchestration layer that feeds data into the rest of the Databricks/Lakehouse Engineer path's lakehouse.
